subject: Recap: TTFT & streaming requirements — FluxCommerce pilot asks
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah@fluxcommerce.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: TTFT & streaming requirements — FluxCommerce pilot asks

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the pilot. Please reply with any corrections.

Key customer goals you shared:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: median < 120ms, 95th <= 320ms for live checkout experiences.
- Sustained concurrency: 400 concurrent streaming sessions for peak shopping windows, with 1,000 QPS burst capacity for promotional spikes.
- Streaming mode: preferring Server-Sent Events (SSE) for browser clients, with WebSocket fallback for mobile SDKs.
- Chunk cadence: short chunks to speed first visible tokens (chunk sizes ~30-80 tokens, pacing 150–250ms between chunks once steady).
- Payload characteristics: average prompt 1.4k tokens (including context), max 6k.

Proposed pilot scope (2 weeks):
1) Canary integration: redirect 0.5% of checkout traffic through a dedicated pilot endpoint.
2) Run synthetic peak ramp: we will test up to 1,200 concurrent active streams using our load harness.
3) Success criteria: TTFT median <120ms and 95th <=320ms in pilot traffic; no more than 3% error rate under load; live chunk cadence within 200ms of target.

What we need from you to kick off:
- Sample payloads (attached flux-payload-samples.json) to seed the pilot harness.
- Desired pilot start date window (we suggested 2027-04-19 in the call).
- Any compliance constraints for logs/traces (PII redaction, log retention).

Next steps
- I will coordinate an internal config doc for the runtime (Aditya, can you draft recommended instance sizing for 1k concurrent SSE streams?).
- Neha will share the observability checklist and the minimal tracer hooks we need from Flux.
- Sarah, once you approve the pilot scope we'll issue a formal pilot SLA (attached) and schedule a short kickoff.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
--
Attachments: flux-payload-samples.json (15KB stub), redwood-pilot-sla-proposal.pdf (34KB stub)
From: Sarah Li <sarah@fluxcommerce.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fluxcommerce.com
Date: 2027-04-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: TTFT & streaming requirements — FluxCommerce pilot asks

Mina — this looks right to me, thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The TTFT median target is a hard product requirement for the checkout UX; 95th at 320ms is acceptable as an upper bound.
- For concurrency: 400 is our baseline expected peak but the marketing team expects occasional flash sales, so please design for 1,000 sustained for 10 minutes as a stress test.
- For chunk cadence: shorter first chunk is important — we prefer the first chunk sized ~20–40 tokens so the UI can render the first visible text quicker.

We can share additional payload variants by EOD Friday. Regarding logs: we cannot ship full PII — we will provide hashed session IDs and request IDs for correlations.

We are good to target the week of 2027-04-19 for the pilot start. Please send the pilot SLA and a short runbook for our infra team to review.

Thanks,
Sarah Li
Head of Product, FluxCommerce
--
Forwarded: ops@fluxcommerce.com confirmed they can support a 0.5% canary and will coordinate CDN invalidations locally.
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-08T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: TTFT & streaming requirements — FluxCommerce pilot asks

Quick internal notes and recommended runtime config for the pilot: 

- Instance sizing: prefer 8x A40-equivalent nodes in a dedicated pool for the 1k burst test, with autoscaling to add 4 nodes at 800 concurrent streams.
- KV cache priming: we should pre-warm by replaying 300 representative sessions (from their sample payloads) to reduce cold-start TTFT variance.
- Streaming config: use SSE default framing with an aggressive first-chunk flush (force flush after 10–20 tokens), then switch to 150–220ms pacing for subsequent chunks.
- Telemetry: sample at 100% for TTFT and 10% full-body token traces; ensure traced spans include kernel selection, batching windows, and network handoff time.

Action items for the team:
- Aditya: produce an internal runbook and node count calc by EOD 2027-04-09.
- Neha: prepare the observability snippet and a minimal tracing patch that Flux can drop into their frontend.
- Ben: draft failover policy for SSE->WebSocket fallback and request routing during CDN hiccups.

I recommend we include an explicit fallback SLO in the pilot: if TTFT 95th > 400ms for more than 3 minutes, automatically downgrade to a lighter model or route to a low-latency replica.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah@fluxcommerce.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-09T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot kickoff confirmed & pilot SLA sent

Sarah — thanks for the quick confirmation. We will treat the TTFT median <120ms and 95th <=320ms as the gating criteria for the pilot. Per Aditya's suggestion, the pilot will include a tiered fallback policy to ensure availability: automatic model downgrade and routing to low-latency replicas when 95th crosses 400ms for >3m.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-sla-proposal.pdf (contains runbook, node sizing, observability checklist).

Planned timeline:
- 2027-04-12: internal runbook and sizing calc delivered (Aditya).
- 2027-04-13: Flux shares final payload variants and redaction plan.
- 2027-04-19: pilot goes live at 0.5% canary.
- 2027-04-21: synthetic peak ramp test and interim results review.
- 2027-04-26: pilot close and go/no-go decision.

Can you confirm the 2027-04-19 kickoff for your side? Once you confirm I will send the DocuSign link for the pilot SLA and schedule the 30-minute kickoff.

Best — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
